name: Ask Sales V5.5 frozen blind human gate

selectionPolicy.sourceRule: Slack cases require an authoritative threaded resolution and a parent source absent from every earlier Ask Sales test and runtime artifact.
selectionPolicy.authorityRule: Exact decision, scope, conditions, finality, recency, and role control. Rich normally outranks Madeline, but context and a materially newer exact decision can control.
exclusions: No question was selected because V3 or V5.5 already answered it well.
Ambiguous or unresolved threads were excluded.
No answer was inferred from peer-only advice.
No client personal data was copied into the fixture.

promotionGate.note: This 20-prompt gate is decision evidence, not automatic authorization to replace production.

reviewQuestions: Which answer is better: A, B, both, or neither?
Does either answer contain a serious operational error?

cases.question: Do the Sunday cohort deadline rules apply to Daymond John / Next Level CEO leads?
cases.goldAnswer: No. Daymond John / Next Level CEO leads are not subject to the main ISTV Sunday cohort deadline, and their acceptance letters should not include that deadline.
requiredConcepts: DJ/NLCEO excluded from Sunday cohort deadline
forbiddenConcepts: apply the main ISTV Sunday deadline to DJ/NLCEO

cases.question: For how long is an episode guaranteed to stay on ISTV?
cases.goldAnswer: The approved ISTV guarantee is five years. Rudy limited that statement to ISTV and identified company sale, company closure, or serious client misconduct as removal boundaries.

cases.question: Can a client buy multiple episodes, and can they choose different seasons or shows?
cases.goldAnswer: Yes. A client can purchase multiple episodes and choose the same season, different seasons, or a mix of shows, with each episode purchased.

cases.question: Is there a minimum time a business must have been operating before it can qualify?
cases.goldAnswer: No fixed minimum time in business was set. A new business can still be approved when it is legitimate, has the means, and otherwise qualifies.

cases.question: A bank transfer failed, but the client already signed for four $2,500 payments. Can I send the official link for that same contracted plan?
cases.goldAnswer: Yes. The official link can be sent when it matches the amount and payment plan already in the signed contract. This does not authorize changing the plan or creating a custom link.

cases.question: A prospect wants me to explain what ROI the episode will generate. What can I promise?
cases.goldAnswer: Do not promise or discuss ROI. The rep must not claim that the episode will generate a particular return.

cases.question: A prospect finished Call 1 but wants Call 2 two weeks later because their investors are traveling. Can I schedule it then?
cases.goldAnswer: No. Call 2 must be scheduled in the same week as Call 1. The stated exceptions are genuine emergencies such as serious illness, a car accident, or a death in the family; investor availability is not one of them.
requiredConcepts: investor travel is not an emergency exception

cases.question: The applicant asked to cancel but did not cancel their booking. Can I remove it from my side, and what reason should I enter?
cases.goldAnswer: Yes. Use the OnceHub link inside the booking to cancel it and enter ‘applicant requested to cancel’ as the reason.

cases.question: A prospect wants to speak directly with a previous cast member before deciding. Can I share someone’s contact details?
cases.goldAnswer: No. Do not provide a cast member’s contact information or arrange direct contact. Use only approved public testimonials or examples.
requiredConcepts: do not share cast member contact information

cases.question: Must every cast member be at least 18?
cases.goldAnswer: No. A younger cast member can be considered if they have a successful business and an adult accompanies them. This is not automatic approval.

cases.question: For America’s Authors, does a published author with a personal brand also need to own a separate business?
cases.goldAnswer: No. For America’s Authors, a published author with a personal brand can qualify without separately owning a business.
requiredConcepts: published author with personal brand can qualify
business ownership not required for this show
forbiddenConcepts: apply the general business-owner requirement without the Authors exception

cases.question: Is a doctor who works for a hospital but does not own a practice a fit for America’s Best Doctors?
cases.goldAnswer: No. For America’s Best Doctors, the stated rule is that a doctor without their own practice is not a good fit.
requiredConcepts: own practice required for America’s Best Doctors
forbiddenConcepts: confuse a nurse with a doctor

cases.question: My client says they were charged twice and wants me to refund one charge. Can you fix it for me?
cases.goldAnswer: The chatbot must not claim it completed or approved a refund. Route the duplicate-charge and refund operation to #sales-finance-requests and avoid sharing sensitive payment details.
approvedBy: Project owner approved current route catalog

cases.question: Please send my client’s greenlight letter before our call today.
cases.goldAnswer: The chatbot cannot send the letter. Direct the rep to #greenlight-requests for the request or urgent status follow-up, without promising timing or outcome.
approvedBy: Project owner approved current route catalog

conversations.title: Natural follow-up: price questions during Call 1

prompts.question: If a prospect asks about cost during Call 1, should I tell them the $10K minimum?
prompts.goldAnswer: No. Do not discuss fees or quote the minimum on Call 1. Explain that cost is discussed on Call 2 after determining whether the studio approves them and which option fits.
requiredConcepts: do not quote cost on Call 1

prompts.question: What if they keep pushing me for an exact breakdown?
prompts.goldAnswer: Do not invent or break down line items. Reiterate that pricing varies and the person is not yet cast; if cost is their only concern and they will not accept the process, the opportunity may not be a fit.
forbiddenConcepts: invent exact travel or promotion costs

conversations.title: Natural follow-up: episode timing and onboarding

prompts.question: After filming, how long does it usually take for a client’s episode to be ready?
prompts.goldAnswer: A useful expectation is roughly four to six months for editing, often around five months depending on how quickly the client gets to Miami. A rush may sometimes be possible in two to three months after filming, but it is not guaranteed.
requiredConcepts: rush two to three months may be possible

prompts.question: And can the client just watch a recording of onboarding instead of attending live?
prompts.goldAnswer: No. The client must attend onboarding live. A rep may attend live or watch a recording if one is available.
requiredConcepts: rep may use recording if available
forbiddenConcepts: client can replace live onboarding with a recording

conversations.title: Natural follow-up: full episode versus clips

prompts.question: Can a cast member upload their full episode to YouTube?
prompts.goldAnswer: No. They may post the trailer, but not the full episode on YouTube.
requiredConcepts: full episode not allowed on YouTube

prompts.question: What about shorter reels chopped from the episode?
prompts.goldAnswer: Yes. Chopped reels from the episode may be posted.
forbiddenConcepts: extend permission to the full episode
